title: How to Prepare for a House Move
excerpt: A simple checklist to help you get organised before moving day.
body:
Moving house is easier when the preparation starts early. This checklist covers the practical points worth sorting out before you contact a moving company for a quotation.

## Start with a plan

- Decide your moving date, or a date range, as early as you can.
- Note the address you are moving from and the address you are moving to, including floors, stairs and lifts.
- Walk through each room and list the large items: beds, wardrobes, sofas, appliances and anything fragile.

## Sort before you pack

Go through your belongings and decide what to keep, donate or discard. A smaller load is easier to handle and can make the job simpler to plan.

## Pack and label

- Keep boxes to a weight you can lift safely.
- Label each box with its room and a short description of the contents.
- Keep important documents, keys, chargers and daily essentials in a bag that travels with you.

## Tell people about the move

Let your landlord or building manager, utility providers and anyone who sends you post know your new address. If your building has rules about moving hours or lift use, check them in advance.

## Share the details when you ask for a quote

When you enquire, tell the company where you are moving from and to, the size of the move, any special items and your preferred date. Clear details help the quotation reflect the actual job.

title: Office Relocation Checklist
excerpt: Points to plan before moving a business to a new office.
body:
An office move affects people, equipment and daily operations, so a little planning goes a long way.

## Before you choose a date

- Confirm the new premises are ready, including access arrangements and any building rules for deliveries and lifts.
- Pick a date that disturbs your work as little as possible, such as a weekend or a quiet period.

## Take stock

- List furniture, desks and storage units that will move.
- List equipment such as computers, printers, phones and network devices.
- Decide what will not be moved and can be sold, donated or discarded.

## Plan the technology

Internet, Wi-Fi, phones and CCTV often need to be working on the first day. Ask early who will disconnect and reconnect them, and where cabling and sockets are in the new space.

## Communicate with your team

Tell staff the date, what they should pack themselves and how to label their items. A short floor plan of the new office makes it easier to place desks and equipment.

## Share the details

When you request a quotation, give the locations, the items to be moved, access conditions at both ends and your preferred date so the work can be planned properly.

title: Preparing to Mount a TV on the Wall
excerpt: What to check before a TV is mounted.
body:
Wall-mounting a TV can free up space, but a few checks help the job go smoothly.

## Know your TV

- Note the screen size and model.
- Check the weight and the mounting hole pattern (often called VESA) in the TV manual or on the manufacturer's website.

## Choose the position

- Decide the viewing height. For most people, the centre of the screen sits near eye level when seated.
- Think about where the power socket, aerial, decoder and other devices will connect.

## Check the wall

Walls differ: brick, concrete, drywall and others each need suitable fixings. Tell the installer what your wall is made of, and mention if there are pipes or electrical cables you know about.

## Bracket

Make sure the bracket matches the TV's size, weight and hole pattern. If you do not have one yet, ask for advice before buying.

## When you ask for a quote

Share your TV size, the planned location, the wall type and whether you already have a bracket.

title: Improving Wi-Fi Coverage at Home
excerpt: Common reasons for weak Wi-Fi and simple things to try.
body:
Slow or patchy Wi-Fi is a common frustration. These points can help you understand what may be happening.

## Router position

- Place the router in a central, open location rather than inside a cupboard or behind a TV.
- Keep it away from thick walls and large metal objects where possible.

## Check what is affected

Is the problem in one room or everywhere? Does it affect all devices or one? Notes like these help narrow down the cause.

## Simple things to try

- Restart the router and the affected device.
- Move closer to the router and compare the speed.
- Check how many devices are connected at once.

## When more equipment may help

Large homes or buildings with thick walls may need extra access points or a wired connection to some rooms. A technician can assess the layout and suggest options.

## When you ask for help

Describe your internet setup, which areas have weak coverage, the type of property and what you have already tried.

title: Planning a CCTV Installation
excerpt: Questions to think about before installing cameras.
body:
Good planning helps a CCTV system do what you need it to do.

## What do you want to cover?

Walk around the property and list the areas that matter to you, such as entrances, parking areas and passages.

## Think about each camera position

- Consider lighting at different times of the day and night.
- Think about height and angle so that cameras are out of easy reach but still give a clear view.
- Check how cables or power will reach each position.

## Recording and viewing

Decide how you want to view footage, for example on a screen at the property or on a phone, and how long you would like recordings to be kept.

## Privacy

Aim cameras at your own property and tell people who regularly use the space, such as staff or tenants, that cameras are in use.

## When you ask for a quote

Share the property type, the number of cameras you have in mind, whether the work is a new installation or a check of an existing system, and the location.

title: Getting Furniture Ready for Assembly
excerpt: A few steps that make flat-pack assembly faster and tidier.
body:
Flat-pack furniture goes together more smoothly when everything is ready beforehand.

## Clear the space

Choose a room with enough floor space to lay out the parts, and place a blanket or cardboard underneath to protect the floor.

## Check the parts

- Keep the instruction sheet and the parts list.
- Count panels, screws and fittings against the list before starting.
- Report any missing or damaged part to the seller early.

## Think about the final position

Heavy items such as wardrobes are easier to assemble close to where they will stand. Measure doorways and ceiling height so the finished piece can be placed.

## For larger jobs

If you have several items, such as beds, wardrobes and desks, list each one with the quantity. Say whether you need assembly, disassembly or both.

## When you ask for a quote

Tell us the type and approximate number of items, the location and your preferred date.
